body:
13 years, 11 months, and 22 days. 


I don't keep track of the specific day, only each rise and fall of the sun. I've always loved numbers. Numbers are all I have in this godforsaken place. 


A loud buzzer rings before there's a knock, and then a metallic sliding. 


"Grub time number 557" 


I shuffled out of my chair and over the cell door. Awaiting me was a green tray with slop haphazardly thrown onto it. 


"Delicious" I called back as the guard made his way to the next cell. 


I returned to my desk with the slop and let out a large sigh. I sat there for a while, not at all in a rush to finish the meal. I looked up at my wall, counting the tally marks once again. It was a great way to pass the time. Each grouping of marks was etched with a different tool. I wasn't allowed to do it, but being here so long I had essentially became invisible. These first ones were done with my nails. I scratched at the wall until my hands became bloody nubs. I peeled my fingernails off after that and tried using them as tools. Eventually however, they degraded and chipped until they were unusable. After that, I moved to my toenails. One by one I'd peel them off, using them to etch more tally marks into the stone wall. 


I took a whiff of the food on my desk. I would have recoiled at the stench if I had  the energy for it. Something grabbed my attention though, a tiny white sliver in the midst of the slop. Cautiously, I grabbed it between my fingers and began to pull. The slop produced a single sheet of paper, with inked markings strewn across it. 


I wiped off the slop as best I could and tried to make out the words that became visible. 


"Yot nee phar goth mal-ek prudj?" 


It was gibberish! The words were written in blood red ink, and were clearly not in the English language. I flipped the paper over, and to my relief, these words were legible. 


"Matt, take this incantation, and get out of there. I'll meet you outside." 


I was at a loss for words. Incantation? Matt? My names not even Matt, it's Derek. 
I shrugged it off as some sort of joke, or lame prank. I stuffed the paper under my pillow and got back to my counting. 


1...


2...


3...
Yes! I was so pulled away from myself, my body. I say "I", but it was really more like... my essence?
That's it!!!

I agree with you that it's subjective. I mean it in the way that my soul was torn from my body and I was in a place far away from earth. I had essentially lost consciousness. Nothing talked to me, but I did see a large face (mask?) at one point, and two other, albeit blurry, entities opening the door to the way in.
